name: kitchen-pudding
description: Local-first recipe store. Every ingredient carries provenance — measured, fitted, or assumed — and a recipe is only as trustworthy as its weakest ingredient. Corrections append beside the original record; the original is never overwritten.
author: USER

data_streams.purpose: Recipe records: title, ingredients (each with qty, unit, provenance), steps
data_streams.description: One JSON file per recipe under the vault. Written once by add(); never rewritten in place.

data_streams.purpose: Append-only correction log per recipe — field, new value, and why
data_streams.description: A .jsonl file per recipe, beside the original, never merged into it. current() replays this over the original to produce the current view; get_original() ignores it entirely.

notes.phase: P0 scaffold — provenance ledger and append-only corrections are real and tested; docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md tracks what's not built yet
notes.not_a_fork: Mealie/Tandoor/KitchenOwl were surveyed and rejected as a base, not for feature reasons but licensing: all three are AGPLv3, which would bind anything built on top of them to the same terms the moment it's run as a service. This is from scratch under Apache-2.0, matching the rest of the store.
notes.mechanism_vs_preference: Not yet enforced in code, only in the data model: provenance (measured/fitted/assumed) is a mechanism claim, checked and testable. Taste, rating, and flavor adjustments are preference and belong in a separate, votable field once one exists — see docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md. Nothing currently lets a preference field overwrite a provenance one, but there's also no schema-level lock stopping it yet; that's an open gate, not a closed one.
notes.aggregation: Recipe.provenance() is min() over ingredients, not a mean and not a majority vote — one assumed quantity in a ten-ingredient recipe makes the whole recipe assumed. CLAUDE.md: 'a result is worth its weakest input, propagated by min().'
